Testimony of Sean Tully, Group Risk Manager
Presented to the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
in Support of LD 1390, Resolve, Directing the Secretary of State to Develop a Plan for a Multiyear Registration System for National Car Rental Companies
Sponsored by Representative Wayne Parry
April 11, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation, my name is Sean Tully. l am here today on behalf of Enterprise Mobility. l am currently in
charge of the Risk Management Department and have been with Enterprise for 24 years. Enterprise has more
than 245 team members with great pay and benefits in 23 offices located throughout Maine. We collect and pay excise, payroll, property and sales taxes in excess of $20 million every year. We continue to be invested in growing our footprint in Maine and have plans to open new locations soon. We are fully vested and invested
in the people and economy of Maine.
Enterprise Mobility is pleased to support LD 1390, Resolve, Directing the Secretary of State to Develop a Plan
for a Multiyear Registration System for National Car Rental Companies. We appreciate Representative Parry
for bringing this bill forward and the bi-partisan group of co-sponsors who have expressed their support.
Enterprise operates in every state and all over the world. increasingly, states are adding rental fleet registration options to their existing vehicle registration program for rental passenger vehicle fleets. This saves rental companies lost revenue due to downtime, improves the availability of vehicles and increases revenue, which yields additional tax dollars to the State. it also saves car rental companies administrative costs associated with annual renewals. Based on our experience in other states, it will save administrative costs for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles as well.
Every state is different, and we do not presume to know the right model for Maine. We know the Secretary of
State's office is working diligently to upgrade its existing vehicle registration system. That is a difficult
challenge. We recognize that this study adds additional time to the BMV's workload. Having said that, this is
the best time to explore a muiti-year registration for rental fleets since a new system can be optimized now to
incorporate this option.
in states that have a muiti-year fleet registration, generally a rental car company elects a common annual
expiration date for all vehicles in its fleet and receives registration stickers for each vehicle in the fleet that are valid for set number of years. At that time, the company pays all registration fees and excise taxes for the fleet
for that term. Typically, the BMV may require the company to produce a current certificate of good standing. if
the company is no longer in good standing or fails to meet the required threshold of vehicles in its fleet, the
BMV terminates their fleet registration and reverts any existing registration credentials to those of non-fleet
vehicles. There are also states that use a permanent sticker or a hard plate that does not expire for fleets.
We believe this study is a valuable first step towards streamlining and improving the process for the car rental
companies that register significant numbers of vehicles in Maine. it will lead to cost savings and increased convenience that will, in turn, lead to more efficient fleet management.
Thank you for the opportunity to testify. l'd be happy to answer any questions.

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORTATION
L.D. 1390 "Resolve, Directing the Secretary of State to Develop a Plan for a Multiyear Registration
System for National Car Rental Companies"
Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State
April ll, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation,
I am providing testimony neither for nor against L.D. 1390 a "Resolve, Directing the Secretary of State to
Develop a Plan for a Multiyear Registration System for National Car Rental Companies."
We would like to commend Representative Parry for recognizing that National Car Rental Companies
bring important and needed business to the State of Maine. Our department shares that viewpoint and understand their role in our economy.

All states recognize the vehicle related fees the companies pay contribute to roadway funding. That is
why there are protections in place to ensure that states equitably collect registration, title and sales tax
funds on their vehicles and no one state can collect more than their share.

29-A MRSA, section 157, allows Maine to enter into the International Registration Plan which creates a
method for states to equitably allocate fees for certain commercial vehicles. It also includes a provision for fee allocations on rental vehicles. Section 905 of the plan states that "Rental passenger car
registrations may be allocated based on the revenue earned in each jurisdiction. Properly allocated rental passenger cars may be rented in any member jurisdiction."
Therefore, each rental company provides an annual report to every state, including Maine BMV. The
report indicates their total revenue earned nationally, their total revenue earned in Maine, and the total
number of vehicles they rent. We are then able to calculate the total number of vehicles each company
must register in Maine. This provision is important to ensure these companies do not register a high proportion of their vehicles in any one state, if they find one state's law favorable over another.
This resolve requires the Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles to develop a plan for the creation of a multiyear registration system for these rental passenger vehicles. It requires the Secretary of State to submit the plan to the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation by December 3,
2025.

The resolve states that the Secretary of State has previously developed and implemented a successful long-term registration program for trailers and semitrailers nationwide pursuant to the Maine Revised Statutes, Title 29-A, section 512 that has generated significant income for the State.
We are opposing this resolve for multiple reasons.
While the long-term trailer program is successful, it's important to remember that excise tax is not required to be collected as a prerequisite to register trailers and semitrailers. Other states, like Texas, who have implemented multiyear registration programs for passenger rental companies do not require an excise tax be paid prior to registration.
It is our understanding that rental companies typically keep passenger vehicles in their fleet for 12-24
months or until the vehicle mileage is around 50,000 to 60,000 miles. If we were to register a large fleet of rental vehicles for multiple years, it is likely that many of those vehicles would be sold before the
registration expires. Currently, rental vehicle companies are cancelling hundreds of registrations every month.
It should be also noted that 80% all registrations are processed in town offiees. These offices use a
computer system provided by 1 of 3 vendors in which the Bureau of Motor Vehicles has approved to process registrations. The towns pay for this software and any upgrades to them. Therefore, when changes are made to the excise tax and/or registration requirements, the vendors charge the towns a fee to modify their software. There will also be a fiscal note to implement any multiyear registration program,
as the BMV will also encounter costs to upgrade our computer system to make the necessary
modifications.
While a multi-year registration may reduce the workload of the vehicle rental companies, it doesn't
reduce the workload for BMV and may increase it, nor does it increase any funding for the state.
In conclusion, the current system in place ensures the appropriate number of these vehicles remain
registered here. Additionally, we simply do not have the capacity to develop the plan required by this bill right now. As you know, for the next year we are replacing about l million sets of license plates which is
a significant undertaking. Also, there are at least 2 other studies that our department must conduct over the next several months and report back to this committee by December or early next year, which is going to significantly stretch our resources.
Thank you for your time today and I will be happy to answer any questions.

Testimony on
M L.D. 1390, "Resolve, Directing the Secretary of State to Develop a Plan for a ultivear Registration System for National Car Rental Companies"
Presented by
Representative Wayne R. Parry
District 140
Transportation Committee Friday, April ll, 2025
Good morning, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation:
I am State Representative Wayne R. Parry, and I proudly represent District 140, Arundel,
Dayton, and a portion of Lyman. It is an honor to appear before you today for the purpose of
Mintroducing L.D. 1390, "Resolve, Directing the Secretary ofState to Develop a Plan for a ultiyear Registration System for National Car Rental Companies."
This bill is very simple. I am looking for the Secretary of State to establish for national car rental companies what we have already implemented with trailer registrations. The trailer
registration system has worked out well. It has generated a great deal of revenue for the State and its Highway Fund.
Every year, national car rental companies buy and register cars in Maine, only to see them go
out of state and get registered elsewhere. I am hoping we can continue to re-register them here,
no matter where they are, and keep that revenue coming back to Maine.
It is my desire for the Secretary of State to work with the industry to develop a plan that
works for the State of Maine and national car rental companies. I leave the details to be worked out by the Secretary.
Thank you for your time, and I would be happy to answer any questions.

District 140

Arundel, Dayton and Lyman (Part)
